answer: Each seat binds to one numbered fold of a shared atlas, and only a walnut block cut from that fold's own grain can print its verification page. The grain runs uniquely through the sheet, so a copied press plate prints a pattern the fold rejects. Each impression splinters the rim, capping it at a few dozen pulls. A binder free to wander between towns arrives unannounced, presses the block on site, trims the edge and signs the fold. Faking a thousand seats needs a thousand distinct walnut blocks, a thousand carving hours and a thousand witnessed pressings, while each seat pays one flat fee.
